goal: Use the set square (triangular prism) to push three blocks (cubes) into a straight, aligned row on the table, without picking any block up, then return the robot arm to its start pose.
instruction_templates: Use the set square to push the three blocks into a straight, aligned row, then reset the robot arm.
success: cube0, cube1 and cube2 (three identical cubes) have their centres (object root origin, xy only) on one line: fit a best line through the three (x,y) centres (SVD principal direction); the maximum perpendicular distance of any centre from that line must be <= 0.008 m (is_in_line threshold=0.008).

Orientation alignment (is_align defaults to True, align_threshold=8): for every one of the three cubes, at least one of its three local axes (x, y or z in world frame) must make an angle < 8 degrees with the fitted line direction (taken as horizontal, z=0), either parallel or anti-parallel (|angle-180| < 8 deg). In practice each cube must be yawed so that one of its faces is parallel to the row within 8 degrees.

All target robots (arms) are back at their episode-start end-effector pose: for each target robot, |dx|,|dy|,|dz| of the real end-pose position vs the start pose are each <= 0.15 m (checked per axis, not Euclidean) and the rotation difference is <= 20 degrees (all_robot_back_to_origin defaults pos_threshold=0.15, rot_threshold=20).

Constraint that must hold during the whole episode (query with aim 0): none of cube0, cube1, cube2 may ever be lifted: if at any checked step a cube's z (root position) exceeds its initial z (recorded right after reset) by more than 0.007 m, the episode is marked failed immediately.
evaluation: Checked after every action (each action = one call to take_action; the reward manager step runs after the action's control sequence has finished executing). The three lift queries are evaluated every step (before the main check); each step where a cube is >0.007 m above its initial z increments its counter, and a counter > 0 (i.e. a single violating step) sets success=False and ends the episode with failure. The main check is one single stage whose conditions (in_line+alignment of the three cubes AND robots back at origin) must all hold simultaneously at the same step; the first such step ends the episode with success (reward 1). Otherwise the episode fails at step_lim=200 actions. final_check is not used. Because the check is evaluated at every step, success is declared at the first moment all conditions hold, so the arm must already be home at the moment the row is aligned (or return home afterwards with the row staying aligned).
objects: target: triangular_prism (the 'set square'), 1 instance, on the table (relative_plane Table), x in [-0.05,0.05], y in [-0.20,-0.15] (m), random yaw within +/-15 degrees. It is a tool for pushing.
cube0, cube1, cube2: three cubes (category cube, index 0, mode 'same' = same cube model for all three), on the table, x in [-0.15,0.15], y in [-0.17,-0.05] (m), random yaw within +/-35 degrees.
needs_memory_or_language: none (the instruction is fixed; the target is any straight row of the three cubes, no particular location or order required).
end_requirements: Both/all target arms must be back within 0.15 m per axis and 20 degrees of their start end-effector pose at the moment of success (see success). Gripper state is not checked.
physics_kind: rigid (rigid cubes and a rigid triangular prism pushed on a table)
notes: Cubes must not be lifted by more than 0.007 m (less than a centimetre) at any step, so push, do not grasp or flip them; even a cube riding up on the set square or tilting could trip this. 0.008 m line tolerance and 8 degree face-alignment tolerance are tight. The row can be at any position/orientation on the table. No requirement of using the set square is checked programmatically, only the geometry. Success is checked right after each action, so a transient alignment while the arm is home also ends the episode as success.
